Cost Insights:


-


Ipe wood decking costs **$14,000** to **$22,000** installed, with your total determined by deck size and labor rates.


-


Deck shape and your site conditions affect costs, and slopes, access, and multi-level layouts require more labor.


-


Budget for railings at $925 on average, plus stairs at $15 to $25 per square foot and UV protectant.


-


[Hiring a local deck building professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/deck-builders/) ensures your backyard project is done well and boosts your overall home value.


In 2026, the national average cost for Ipe wood decking installation is **$18,000** . Most homeowners spend between **$14,000** and **$22,000** , with deck size and labor rates driving most of the spread.


## **Ipe Wood Decking Cost Factors: What Affects the Price?**


Several factors shape the final cost of an Ipe wood decking project, so connecting with a[local deck builder near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/deck-builders/) is the best way to get an accurate quote for your specific backyard. Deck size, site conditions, foundation requirements, and labor rates all play a role in where your total lands.


Price Notice


In November 2024, three genera in the Ipe family ( *Handroanthus* , *Roseodendron* , and *Tabebuia* ) were added to the CITES Appendices of species with a threat of endangerment. Trade of Ipe is now more strictly regulated with increased pricing.


### **Deck Size**


Deck size is one of the most direct cost drivers for Ipe wood, ranging from **$5,000 to $8,000** for a smaller 10x10 space up to **$20,000 to $32,000** or more for a 20x20 layout. Because this[decking material](https://www.angi.com/articles/good-material-key-long-lasting-decks.htm) is dense, time-consuming to work with, and requires specialized equipment, larger square footage quickly translates to higher material and labor costs. The table below shows how installed Ipe prices break down across common deck dimensions:

### **Deck Shape**


Deck shape directly affects labor costs, and choosing a standard rectangle or square keeps your bill lower by avoiding the additional fees that come with cutting unique angles or curves. Homeowners with more flexibility in their budget can opt for raised or multi-layered Ipe designs, which offer greater visual impact but require more complex, time-intensive work from your contractor.


### **Foundation Installation**


If your property does not already have a foundation in place, you can expect to pay **$5 to $15 per square foot** to add one, with the final cost depending on whether the work involves only pouring concrete or also requires building a wooden substructure beneath the deck.


### **Site Preparation**


Site preparation costs vary widely depending on what your property requires before construction can begin. Demolishing an existing deck adds labor costs that your[decking pro](https://www.angi.com/nearme/deck-builders/) can quote directly, and if the land needs leveling first, budget around **$2,200** as an average[cost to regrade your yard](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-yard-leveling-cost.htm) .


### **Labor**


Labor typically accounts for 15% to 25% of the total project cost, with professional deck contractors charging **$15 to $35 per square foot** . Site conditions such as sloped terrain or second-story placement increase the complexity of the work and push labor costs toward the higher end of that range.


### **Location and Availability**


Where you live affects both labor rates and material costs for Ipe decking, since regions with a higher cost of living typically see higher contractor rates for the specialized tools and expertise this wood requires. Ipe is sourced from Central and South America, so homeowners in remote areas should also factor in shipping and transportation costs that can add to the overall price.

## **Comparing Ipe to Other Decking Materials: Which Fits Your Budget?**


Since Ipe wood is now threatened with endangerment, you may wish to look at[alternative decking materials](https://www.angi.com/articles/best-wood-for-decks.htm) , which range from **$3,600 to $12,000** overall. Here's how other options compare:


Deck Material Average Cost Range in 2026 Pros Cons


Ipe $14,000–$22,000 Highly durable and long-lasting; requires little maintenance; resists rot, insects, and moisture International trade is regulated, which comes with higher costs, less availability, and ethical concerns


Cedar $3,600–$9,000 Relatively affordable; resists rot and insects; classic wood look; easy to install Needs regular maintenance; less durable than other options; scratches easily


Pressure-Treated Wood $4,000–$12,000 Accessible for homeowners; can be customized; easy to work with Shorter lifespan than Ipe and composite decking contains chemicals; requires more maintenance


Composite $5,400–$11,500 Lasts a long time; available in a wide range of colors and styles Might be more costly than wood decking; may look artificial


### **Cedar**


[Cedar decking](https://www.angi.com/articles/cedar-decking-prices.htm) is more budget-friendly and easier to install than Ipe. While Ipe is highly durable and more resistant to rot, insects, and moisture, it's an endangered species, which increases cost, lowers availability, and raises ethical concerns. Cedar still resists insect and rot damage, plus it is more sustainable and readily available with no wait time.


### **Pressure-Treated Wood**


Ipe will last longer than[pressure-treated wood decking](https://www.angi.com/articles/pressure-treated-decking-cost.htm) , but it's also more expensive. Pressure-treated wood isn't cheap either, but it's much more accessible for homeowners to purchase. However, pressure-treated wood requires more maintenance, including regular cleaning, staining, and resealing.


### **Composite**


Ipe is more expensive than[composite decking](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-composite-decking-cost.htm) , though it's slightly more durable. Both materials, however, can last for a long time. To that end, Ipe requires a bit more maintenance than composite. Ipe is also generally considered to be the better-looking material, but composite is available in a wide range of colors and styles.


## **Additional Ipe Wood Decking Costs to Consider**


LUNAMARINA / iStock / Getty Images Plus / Getty Images


Some other features are necessary to complete the space, and they're often not included in the average cost of Ipe decking.


### **Railings**


Installing or[replacing exterior railings](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-should-it-cost-replace-porch-railings.htm) costs an average of **$925** , including labor and materials, and adds both safety and visual appeal to your finished deck. Upgrading to premium options is also an option, with[glass or cable railings](https://www.angi.com/articles/update-railing-your-deck.htm) running **$150 to $250 per linear foot** for cable and **$200 to $450 per linear foot** for glass.


Railing Type Average Cost in 2026


Standard railings $925


Cable railings $150–$250 per lin. ft.


Glass railings $200–$450 per lin. ft.


### **Deck Stairs**


[Building deck stairs](https://www.angi.com/articles/installing-deck-stairs-4-steps.htm) costs **$15 to $25 per square foot** , including labor and materials, with the final price driven by design complexity, height, and the number of steps. For raised or multi-level Ipe decks, stairs are a required expense rather than an optional upgrade.


### **Staining or Painting**


Applying a UV protectant to your Ipe deck costs **$1 to $2.50 per square foot** and is the recommended coating approach for this dense hardwood, since standard stains do not penetrate or change the color the way they would on lighter wood. The protectant's primary job is to prevent sun fading and preserve the wood's natural appearance over time.


### **Electricity**


If you want to power lighting or outdoor speakers on your new Ipe deck, the[cost to install an outdoor electrical outlet](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-install-outdoor-outlet.htm) averages around **$225** . This is a straightforward add-on that significantly expands how you can use the space after dark.


### **Maintenance**


Oiling oil runs **$60 to $90 per gallon** for a DIY approach, or you can hire a professional to handle it for **$2.50 to $5.50 per square foot** . Ipe wood is a naturally[low-maintenance decking material](https://www.angi.com/articles/smart-deck-renovations-cut-costs-and-maintenance.htm) thanks to its density and built-in resistance to rot and insects, giving homeowners the choice to oil it annually to preserve the rich brown tone or leave it untreated for a weathered silver-gray look.

## **Why You Should Hire a Decking Pro**


Installing decking is something you can do yourself, and tackling everything from start to finish would save you an average of between $2,700 and $4,500 on labor alone. However, hiring a professional[deck builder near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/deck-builders/) is worth the investment to ensure a professional appearance, good structural stability, and maximum deck longevity.


### **Here's why it's ideal to hire a decking pro**


Paying thousands of dollars for labor may not seem like it's worth it, but there are a few important benefits that come with hiring a pro.


-


Ipe is a very expensive material, and hiring a pro means a lower risk of material damage and unnecessary waste during the installation process.


-


A pro can install a solid deck foundation if you don't already have one, which means good structural stability and durability.


-


Professionals will pull permits for deck installation to make sure your project is legal and up to code.


-


Pros can recommend finishes and maintenance for your ipe wood deck based on your climate and location for maximum deck lifespan.


### **If you want to DIY your Ipe wood deck installation**


DIYing an ipe wood deck from start to finish isn't ideal, but there are some smaller tasks you can tackle yourself if you're handy and want to contribute to the work and save on labor costs.


-


Consider removing your old decking material, if applicable, and hauling it away before your pro arrives.


-


Seal or finish your decking after the installation, provided you've consulted with your pro on materials and application technique.


-


If installing a deck from scratch, clear and level the area to prepare for foundation pouring.


## **How to Save on Ipe Decking Costs**


Ipe isn't the most budget-friendly material, so don't expect to cut your project costs in half with one magical tip. However, there are a few ways to save if you're trying to get the most bang for your buck.


-


Choose a classic shape, like a square or rectangle, for your deck. A simple deck shape means lower labor costs.


-


Get more than one quote from contractors, and don't just choose the cheapest quote. Some contractors may offer deals on materials, better warranties, or savings on different parts of the project. Look at pro quotes as a whole rather than just focusing on the price.


-


Order your Ipe wood decking in bulk during the fall or winter when prices are lower. You'll cut costs due to seasonality and may even save by buying in bulk.


Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro


-


Provide a to-scale drawing of your yard area and the deck, including desired design elements.


-


Ask your pro about where they’re sourcing the wood from to ensure safe and legal materials and high-quality decking.


-


Discuss any add-on services you’d like, including railing and stair installation.


-


Make sure you’re clear about who is responsible for finishing the deck and the recommended timeline.

Frequently Asked Questions


Ipe wood can last up to 75 years with minimal maintenance because its own oils help to preserve it. However, to get the most out of your Ipe wood deck, you should perform some routine maintenance, including regular cleaning, sweeping of leaves and debris, and rinsing spills with a hose. It’s also important to repair any deep scratches as soon as you spot them and reseal the deck annually to protect against scratches and scuffs.


Yes, Ipe is more expensive than Trex decking—both in terms of materials and installation (plus, Ipe trees are endangered). On average, Ipe decking costs $10 to $25 per square foot, while[Trex decking costs](https://www.angi.com/articles/what-cost-trex-decking.htm) $5 to $12 per square foot. Because Ipe is harder to work with, the price of installation is higher, too. For Ipe decking, you’ll pay between $20 and $45 per square foot for labor. However, with Trex decking, the labor costs range from $8 to $22 per square foot.


Yes, Ipe wood is a popular high-end choice for pool decking. It repels water and is naturally slip-resistant. It's not susceptible to mold, mildew, or rot, either, so it lasts longer and is cleaner and more hygienic than other popular decking materials. However, remember that due to its status, it is a very high-cost wood, and you might find that an alternative would serve you just as well for significantly less.


No, you don't need to stain Ipe decking, although you can if you want to change the color. You will, however, need to apply a UV coating if you don't want the natural color to fade. Speak to a[deck staining specialist near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/deck-staining/) to discuss the best options if you want to stain your decking. And remember that you’ll need to seal your Ipe wood deck annually to protect it from scratches and Mother Nature.
